name: OSCAR
product: OSCAR (Open Source CPAP Analysis Reporter) by the OSCAR Team

evidence.says: The OSCAR Team dates 2.1.1 to October 31, 2026 and offers a separate Apple Silicon ARM disk image requiring macOS 14 or later.

name: Verizon Utility Application - LG
product: LG Electronics Verizon Utility Application for the LG Software Upgrade Assistant

evidence.says: Verizon's instructions identify the Mac and PC Software Upgrade Assistant used to update LG devices.
LG ended its Software Upgrade Assistant service for North American Verizon LG devices on June 30, 2024.

limitation: The final Mac client version and its architecture are unverified.
notes: The historical scan covers version 2.1.0.

name: JDownloader Installer
product: JDownloader 2 installer by the JDownloader project (AppWork)

evidence.says: The project's download page identifies this bundle as the JDownloader 2 installation package and offers Apple Silicon installers for current macOS versions.

notes: The installer is separate from the installed JDownloader 2 application.

name: Grammarly Editor
product: Grammarly Editor, the standalone desktop document editor by Grammarly

evidence.says: The article reproduces the in-app retirement notice and dates the end of the standalone Mac and Windows Editor to March 20, 2024.
The vendor markets its current Mac download as a writing assistant that works inside other apps, with a separate Docs link.

limitation: The final desktop Editor version and its architecture were not verified.
notes: The Editor moved to the browser in March 2024. The current Grammarly for Mac writing assistant is a separate product.

name: Universe Installer
product: Red Giant Universe suite installer by Red Giant, now Maxon

evidence.says: Maxon describes Universe as an installable Red Giant suite and says the dedicated suite installers were replaced by a unified installer in 2024.

notes: The scanned 3.3.0 bundle installs host-application plugins.

name: Magzster
product: Magzster, a generated Fluid 2 website wrapper built with Todd Ditchendorf’s Fluid

evidence.says: Fluid lets users enter their own website URL and app name to generate a separate macOS app bundle.
The scan identifies the executable as FluidApp and the bundle as com.fluidapp.FluidApp2.Magzster.

limitation: The URL chosen when creating this particular wrapper is unknown.
notes: The App Store’s Magzter app is a separate product.

name: OpenAudible
product: OpenAudible audiobook manager by the OpenAudible project

evidence.says: The official download page identifies the current macOS DMG as a universal binary for Intel and Apple Silicon.
The publisher marks 5.3 as the latest release and dates it November 22, 2026.

name: Wondershare AllMyTube
product: Wondershare AllMyTube for Mac

evidence.says: Wondershare’s Mac guide states that distribution in Japan ended on August 30, 2017 and that feature upgrades ended.

limitation: The final global Mac version and its executable architecture were not verified.
notes: Wondershare directs users to UniConverter for the same video-download use case.

name: Quitter
product: Quitter for Mac by Marco Arment

evidence.says: Marco Arment links the current Quitter.zip, whose Quitter.app/Contents/MacOS/Quitter executable was inspected and contains x86_64 and arm64 slices with bundle version 1.0 build 108.

limitation: The exact release date of build 108 is unverified.
notes: The current universal download keeps the same marketing version as earlier builds.

name: RapidClick
product: RapidClick by Pilotmoon Software (Nick Moore)

evidence.says: Pilotmoon identifies the current RapidClick 1.5.1 as a universal app for Apple Silicon and Intel and dates it May 19, 2021.

name: Uninstall CylancePROTECT
product: CylancePROTECT uninstaller bundled with Arctic Wolf Aurora Protect Desktop

evidence.says: Arctic Wolf identifies Uninstall CylancePROTECT.app as the bundled macOS utility for removing its endpoint agent.

notes: The CylancePROTECT desktop agent has its own listing.

name: RemNote
product: RemNote desktop by RemNote Inc.

evidence.says: RemNote offers a dedicated Apple Silicon download alongside the separate Intel Mac build.
RemNote’s Apple Silicon update manifest lists ARM64 Mac ZIP and DMG builds of 1.30.6 with a November 25, 2026 release timestamp.

name: cloudLibrary
product: cloudLibrary standalone desktop client for Mac by bibliotheca, now part of OCLC

evidence.says: Bibliotheca's user guide identifies the original standalone PC and Mac reader.
A subscribing public library confirms that the dedicated Mac and PC app was withdrawn and directs desktop readers to their browsers.
The current CloudLibrary site directs desktop patrons to the online reader and presents separate app options for mobile devices.

limitation: The exact final standalone Mac version and its executable architecture were not verified.
notes: The CloudLibrary service continues through the web reader and mobile apps.

name: Day-O
product: Day-O, the menu-bar clock and calendar by Shaun Inman

evidence.says: I inspected Day-O.app/Contents/MacOS/Day-O in this official archive and verified an x86_64-only Mach-O and bundle version 3.0.1.
MacUpdater identifies 3.0.1 as the Intel release dated April 10, 2020.
A user reports that the April 2020 Day-O 3 release runs on an Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 12.3.1, although its Preferences window fails to open.

limitation: A user reports that Preferences does not open on macOS 12.3.1.

name: etesync-dav
product: EteSync DAV, the local CalDAV and CardDAV adapter by the EteSync project

evidence.says: The project tags 0.35.1 as its latest release and publishes new prebuilt binaries.
I inspected etesync-dav.app/Contents/MacOS/etesync-dav inside mac-etesync-dav.zip and verified an x86_64-only Mach-O.

limitation: Rosetta operation was not verified for the released bundle.
notes: The app’s Info.plist reports a placeholder version 0.0.0. The enclosing release asset is tagged 0.35.1.

name: MiniPlay
product: MacAppsters’ Pandora client distributed under names including Music Streamer and PanRadio

evidence.says: The scanner records a Music Streamer bundle with the supplied MacAppsters identifier and PanRadio executable.
Apple’s U.S. lookup returns no current result for this exact bundle ID.

limitation: I found no current release or reliable vendor statement of retirement or compatibility.
notes: Daft Logic Studio’s MiniPlay for Spotify & iTunes is a separate app.

name: CylancePROTECT
product: CylancePROTECT Desktop agent (CylanceUI), now Arctic Wolf Aurora Protect Desktop

evidence.says: Arctic Wolf lists x86_64 in the processor requirements and explicitly requires Rosetta on Apple silicon.
The vendor's macOS compatibility matrix lists the 3.3 agent series as the newest supported series.
Current Aurora Protect documentation retains CylanceUI.app as the name of its macOS UI bundle.

limitation: The latest 3.3 patch and the architecture of each separately bundled component were not verified.
notes: The Rosetta requirement applies to the documented desktop agent as distributed.

name: Advanced Uninstall Manager
product: Advanced Uninstall Manager by Systweak Software

evidence.says: Apple's US Mac App Store lookup identifies the exact bundle ID and returns version 3.4 with a current-version release date of October 16, 2026.
Systweak directs Mac users to the Mac App Store and gives a minimum macOS version without stating the executable architecture.

limitation: No architecture declaration or inspectable official binary was found for version 3.4.
notes: The Intel scan covers the older version 2.5.

name: DevSwatch
product: DevSwatch (Developer's Swatch) by Aubree Kendall

evidence.says: MacUpdater identifies the exact bundle, says it left the Mac App Store and reports Intel and Apple Silicon architectures for version 1.3 build 4.
Apple's US Mac App Store lookup returns zero results for the precise bundle identifier.

limitation: The vendor did not confirm removal and the archived architecture metadata could not be independently reproduced.
notes: The archive reports a universal final build, while the input scan for 1.30 did not find an arm64 slice.

name: Fuse
product: Fuse Studio by Fusetools AS, later hosted by the Fuse Open community

evidence.says: The Fuse team announced the stable 1.9.0 release on May 28, 2018 and explained that Fusetools AS would no longer issue official updates.
The Fuse Community installation discussion states that the old Fusetools Studio desktop product is no longer maintained.
The community release archive retains the old stable release and the later 1.10.0 release candidate.

limitation: The final stable Mac installer was not inspected and its binary architecture was not independently established.
notes: Fuse Open's mobile framework and Fuse X development are separate from the original stable desktop release.

name: fre:ac - free audio converter
product: fre:ac audio converter by the fre:ac project (Robert Kausch)

evidence.says: The project lists freac-1.1.7-macos11.dmg for Intel and Apple Silicon, and inspection of its freac.app/Contents/MacOS/freac executable confirmed x86_64 and arm64 slices in version 1.1.7.
The release announcement dates fre:ac 1.1.7 to March 5, 2023.

notes: Use the macOS 11 or later download for Apple Silicon.

name: Dresden Files Co-op Card Game
product: Dresden Files Cooperative Card Game by Hidden Achievement LLC

evidence.says: The developer lists the Mac App Store and Steam as official macOS distribution channels.
The Mac App Store lists version 2.1.4 dated December 4, 2025 and describes an engine update without identifying the executable architectures.
The publisher lists Intel and Apple Silicon processors in its Mac requirements without specifying native execution or Rosetta.

limitation: The current Mac executable architecture and whether Steam compatibility requires Rosetta were not established.

name: KeePassX
product: KeePassX password manager by the KeePassX team

evidence.says: The project confirms that development stopped and still offers the final Mac binary as version 2.0.3.
The project’s news archive dates version 2.0.3 to October 8, 2016.
I inspected KeePassX.app/Contents/MacOS/KeePassX in the final disk image and verified an x86_64-only Mach-O, with the matching bundle ID and version 2.0.3.

notes: The developers direct users to the separate KeePassXC fork. The final Mac bundle was Intel-only.

name: SD Card Formatter
product: SD Memory Card Formatter by the SD Association and Tuxera

evidence.says: The SD Association lists version 5.0.4, credits Tuxera, and says some Apple Silicon users might be prompted to install Rosetta.
I inspected SD Card Formatter.app/Contents/MacOS/SD Card Formatter in the official package and verified a universal Mach-O with arm64 and x86_64 slices and bundle build 5.0.4-c3c2efc.

limitation: The vendor’s Rosetta caveat remains in the requirements, and installation and runtime were not tested.

name: Solar App
product: Logitech Solar App for the Wireless Solar Keyboard K750 for Mac

evidence.says: Apple identifies the currently listed App Store version as 1.00, dated August 17, 2011, with the exact Logitech bundle ID.
A 2021 review of the Logitech App Store title reports that the app fails on an M1 Mac with macOS Big Sur.
Logitech identifies Solar App as the utility used to detect the K750 and assess its illumination and charge.

limitation: The reported failure covers the App Store build on M1 and Big Sur. The separately scanned direct build 1.0.40 and newer macOS releases were not verified.

name: Display Menu
product: Display Menu by Milch im Gemüsefach / Thorsten Karrer

evidence.says: The developer’s release history records native Apple Silicon support from 2.2.4 and identifies 2.2.6 as the current release.
Apple’s lookup identifies version 2.2.6, the exact bundle ID, and its January 5, 2026 release date.
The current 2.2.6 entry specifies both Intel 64 and Apple Silicon architectures.
The versioned 2.2.6 listing identifies it as a universal binary.

name: Stack
product: Stack 3 browser by Stack (original getstack.app edition)

evidence.says: MacUpdater identifies the exact bundle as the Stack browser, explicitly marks it discontinued, and lists final documented build 3.43.2 with Intel and Apple Silicon support.
The publisher’s current browser download page points to Stack Next SE beta packages, including a separate Apple Silicon build.
The name-matched cask describes TransIP’s cloud storage app and identifies it with the nl.transip.stack bundle ID.

limitation: The publisher’s original Stack 3 download and a first-party end-of-life notice were not located.
notes: The last documented Stack 3 release was native according to MacUpdater. Stack Next SE is a successor edition.

name: VidConvert
product: VidConvert for Mac by Reggie Ashworth

evidence.says: The exact bundle’s catalog entry identifies Reggie Ashworth and records 1.7.2 as an Intel release dated February 26, 2017.
MacUpdate lists the same Intel 64 release and documents user reports that its official conversion-engine download disappeared.

limitation: An official end-of-life notice and Rosetta behavior for the last known release were not verified.
notes: The original vendor product and download URLs now lead to unrelated content. The final documented release was Intel-only.

name: Convert It
product: Convert It macOS menu-bar unit converter by Chimp Studios LLC

evidence.says: Chimp Studios’ founder identifies Convert It as a Mac app developed and supported during his time at the studio.
The exact bundle’s catalog entry dates Intel build 1.6.1 to March 30, 2017 and gives the Mac App Store as its distribution channel.
Apple’s current US Mac software catalog returns no listing for the exact bundle ID.
Apple’s current Canadian Mac software catalog also returns no listing for the exact bundle ID.

limitation: A formal end-of-life notice and any availability confined to other storefronts were not verified.
notes: The last documented version was Intel-only.

name: mwplay
product: MWPlay desktop IPTV player by Techex Ltd

evidence.says: The historical scan identifies version 1.10.0 of the Qt-based Techex desktop bundle as an Intel build.
Techex advertises macOS viewing clients under its current tx iptv family without listing the original desktop bundle, release version, or executable architecture.
Apple identifies the public MWPlay 1.7.3 mobile release as uk.co.techex.play, a separate bundle from the scanned desktop application.

limitation: No current release or architecture could be established for the scanned desktop bundle.
notes: The iPad app’s availability on Apple Silicon is separate from the desktop client.

name: CZUR Shine
product: CZUR Shine legacy scanner application by CZUR

evidence.says: CZUR's Shine Ultra download page data lists Shine 2.3.2, dated September 21, 2025, as the legacy compatible download under the Mac Intel option.
CZUR Japan's Shine Ultra Pro software specifications say that an M1 Mac requires Rosetta.
CZUR says its unified native scanner software covers the Shine hardware family.

limitation: The legacy image exceeds the inspection limit and its runtime was not tested here.
notes: The current native downloads are branded CZUR Scanner and CZUR Image+; their architecture does not establish an arm64 slice in the separately named legacy Shine app.

name: Doit.im
product: Doit.im for Mac by Snoworange Technology International Limited

evidence.says: The vendor's Mac App Store listing shows Snoworange as the developer and lists version 4.2.3 without an architecture declaration.
The vendor still presents a Mac client on the product homepage but its download link points to a 4.0.1 filename.
The official FAQ describes the Snoworange Mac client without identifying a current Apple Silicon build.

limitation: The current build and architecture across vendor and store channels are unresolved, and no reliable Apple Silicon runtime evidence was found.
notes: The historical scan is for 4.2.6, newer than the displayed App Store version.

name: Kitsas
product: Kitsas bookkeeping software by Kitsas Oy, with macOS builds maintained by Petri Aarnio

evidence.says: Kitsas Oy links version 5.11.1 for macOS 11 or later and identifies Petri Aarnio as the Mac build maintainer.
The Mac maintainer tagged Kitsas 5.11.1 on January 18, 2026 and published a DMG without an architectural label.

limitation: The Mac release has no documented architecture and the 221 MB DMG exceeds the brief's binary-inspection limit.

name: Better Rename 9
product: Better Rename 9, the legacy publicspace.net Mac App Store edition of A Better Finder Rename 9

evidence.says: Publicspace.net identifies Better Rename 9 as the Mac App Store edition and explains the move to its separately distributed version 10.
Apple's US store lookup returns zero results for the legacy App Store bundle ID.
Publicspace.net lists 9.54 in the legacy downloads; inspection of its ABFRX9.dmg found an x86_64 main executable for the distinct direct-download bundle net.publicspace.abfr9.

limitation: The final version and architecture specific to the removed App Store bundle were not established.
notes: The scanned App Store build 9.52 was nonnative; the observed Intel-only direct edition is version 9.54 and uses a different bundle ID.

name: Mini vMac
product: Mini vMac Macintosh emulator by Paul C. Pratt’s Gryphel Project

evidence.says: The stable project download labels Mini vMac 36.04 for modern Intel Macs as x86-64 and points Apple Silicon users to the beta.
The developer says the Intel x86-64 release should work through Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon running Big Sur.
The official project news announces the release of 36.04 on October 28, 2018.
The upstream 37.03 beta download lists a separately built Apple Silicon binary.

limitation: The Rosetta statement covers Big Sur, and newer macOS releases were not tested.
notes: The current stable release is Intel-only. Native Apple Silicon support is available in the official 37.03 beta.

name: HDHomeRun
product: HDHomeRun Mac TV viewer by SiliconDust USA, Inc.

evidence.says: I inspected HDHomeRun.app/Contents/MacOS/HDHomeRun inside hdhomerun.pkg in this vendor installer and verified the exact bundle, version 20260326 build 21, and both arm64 and x86_64 Mach-O slices.
SiliconDust records the March 26, 2026 package release and documents native ARM64 support for its Mac viewer starting in release 20221023.
The current Mac App Store listing includes a developer response confirming the Mac viewer has native M1 support.

limitation: The directly distributed Mach-O was inspected. The newer Mac App Store build was not independently inspected.
notes: SiliconDust’s current downloads page directs users to the Mac App Store for the viewer and lists the tuner utilities separately.

name: Silicio
product: Silicio: Widgets + Mini Player by Jan Bolz

evidence.says: Jan Bolz’s Mac App Store listing identifies 3.7.3 as the current version, released July 27, 2026.
Desktop Insights records a measured July 27 scan of the version 3.7.3 macOS binary with arm64 and x86_64 architectures.
Softpedia also lists Silicio 3.7.3 as a universal binary.

limitation: The architecture is based on a published scan of the current binary. MacUpdate’s catalogue also lists 3.7.3 but labels it Intel 64.

name: RemotePCSuite
product: RemotePC Full-Suite for Mac by IDrive, originally Pro Softnet

evidence.says: IDrive distributes the Mac RemotePC Full-Suite on the product download page.
IDrive’s site metadata supplies the current Mac Full-Suite download, version 7.7.49, and release date November 25, 2026.

I inspected RemotePCSuite.app/Contents/MacOS/RemotePCSuite in the official installer’s ApplicationDirectory package and verified a universal x86_64 and arm64 Mach-O with the matching bundle ID and version 7.7.49.

name: Araxis Merge
product: Araxis Merge by Araxis Ltd.

evidence.says: Araxis identifies 2026.1 as the current release, dates it September 23, 2026 and links its macOS installer.
Static inspection of Araxis Merge.app/Contents/MacOS/Araxis Merge in the official 2026.1 image found a universal Mach-O with x86_64 and arm64 slices.

notes: This version requires macOS 15 or later.

name: ColorNavigator 7
product: ColorNavigator 7, EIZO Corporation’s ColorEdge monitor calibration software

evidence.says: EIZO offers ColorNavigator 7 version 7.2.9B and identifies macOS 27 support and the end of Ventura support as its release changes.
EIZO’s update history dates the 7.2.9B software release to October 7, 2026.
A ColorEdge owner reports native Apple Silicon support in the update and shows the 7.2.9.6 in-app notes matching EIZO’s 7.2.9B change list.
EIZO explicitly documents native Apple Silicon support for the earlier 7.1.9 build and identifies specific legacy calibration sensors that require Rosetta.

limitation: The current 7.2.9B installer was not inspected, and architecture evidence for that build comes from a first-hand report.
notes: The compatible version varies by monitor, calibration sensor, and macOS release.
